methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Tech Researchers Use AI to Gauge Manufacturing Water Needs - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI research on manufacturing water needs demonstrates deep technical capability concentrated in the New River Valley academic hub, but signals remain research-focused rather than distributed implementation across Virginia's manufacturing base.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community-level AI education and broad participation, signaling intentional distribution strategy to build grassroots fluency beyond elite tech corridors.

signals.title: How AI is changing what happens to Hampton Roads' trash - The Suffolk News-Herald
signals.signal_reading: AI deployment in Hampton Roads waste management represents shallow, platform-delivered adoption—operational efficiency gains without requiring deep local AI capability development, fitting the 'software does it' pattern.

signals.title: Hospital becomes first to use AI to spot infections early - norfolkneradio.com
signals.signal_reading: Hospital's early adoption of AI infection detection shows concentrated institutional capability in Hampton Roads healthcare sector, but single-institution deployment highlights lack of regional diffusion mechanisms for specialized AI competency.

signals.title: Virginia Tech's AI Model Aims to Ease Drought Water Conflicts - AGDAILY
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's drought water conflict AI model showcases deep research capability addressing statewide agricultural needs, but development remains centralized in Blacksburg rather than distributed to farming communities in Shenandoah Valley or Southside who face the actual water conflicts.
